correctness.rationale: For a nonempty pattern the relevant window has L-|v|+1 possible starts when L>=|v|, including overlaps. Complete periods contribute the same count; the residual arc of length r has range at most min(r,p-r,t,p-t) for t occurrence residues. Reaching k=floor(p/2) forces t and r into {k,p-k}; for every even or odd case a maximizing arc must be exactly the starts or a minimizing arc exactly their complement, and a block of either permitted size attains the bound. For k>=2 adjacent starts force a one-letter power, and its start block comes from a single cyclic run, with the second run too short to contribute. Conversely c^(R1-k+1) realizes a start block of size k when the run gap is at least k. The singleton-letter argument covers p=2,3. A two-run word is primitive by its single cyclic 0-to-1 transition. The proof covers all pattern lengths. In line 33 'exceeds' should read 'is at least'; even equal runs are covered by the displayed non-strict criterion, so this wording does not invalidate the theorem. Independent direct overlapping-window counts passed for 1508 primitive binary/ternary periods (replay: python /workspace/branches/independent_replay.py 2); these finite checks are not the proof. The frozen checker and output were inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: Uniform factor balance is an established invariant. The theorem makes least period a calibrated sharp benchmark across alphabets and gives a direct cyclic-run test for exactly when no smaller uniform constant works. The classification applies even though the definition ranges over all lengths and patterns; it is stronger than a routine proof that a periodic word is uniformly factor-balanced.
